correctness.rationale: With w(z)=r+(1-r)z, the common-height overlap is bounded slice by slice by |B|min(w(z),w(2s-z))^(d-1); centered nested dilates attain it. At z=s, equal positive dilates displaced by 2u for u≠0 cannot agree up to a null set (convexity, nonempty interior and boundedness), and continuity gives strict loss on an interval. This proves axial uniqueness even with flat faces. The axial volume is 2|B| times the integral of w^(d-1) from max(0,2s-1) to s; end heights give zero, while the midpoint has positive volume. For r<1 the lower half increases strictly; on the upper half the derivative has the sign of a^(d-1)-2(2a-1)^(d-1), a=w(s). The ratio (2a-1)/a is strictly increasing, so the unique possible interior maximum is at a_d, and is feasible precisely when (1+r)/2≤a_d. At the crossing the sign is negative immediately to its right, still giving uniqueness. The antiderivative gives total volume |B|(1-r^d)/(d(1-r)); 2[a_d^d-(q_da_d)^d]=a_d^(d-1) yields the first ratio, the midpoint gives the second, and the prism is centrally symmetric with a unique center. These arguments also cover the cone and affine shears. The packaged script describes finite regression checks only; the analytic proof supplies the universal result.
